chunks: Ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Muhammad ibn Abi Hamzah, and Husayn ibn Uthman, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) who said:
Pride is the robe of Allah, so whoever attempts to take Allah’s robe from Him, Allah will throw him face-first into the Fire.

key_terms.أَكَبَهُ: He threw him face-down (on the face)
key_terms.الْكِبْرُ: Arrogance, pride (as a divine attribute vs. human vice)
key_terms.رِدَاءُ اللَّهِ: The robe of Allah (metaphor for exclusive divine attribute)
key_terms.نَازَعَ: To contest, vie with, or dispute

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual consequence of claiming arrogance for oneself in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Kitab al-Zuhd*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) identifies arrogance as the exclusive 'garment' of God, implying that human pride is a usurpation of divine majesty. This concept is deeply rooted in Shia theology, where *kibr* is not merely a sin but a fundamental rejection of God's sovereignty, leading to the specific punishment of being cast face-down in Hell as a sign of humiliation. The imagery underscores the contrast between God's elevated status and the lowly state of the arrogant.
